title: Mini Calculator App
story: Your phone's calculator app has dozens of buttons behind a sleek interface. But at its core, each button is just a function. You'll build the complete engine — six operations, each a clean function, wired together into a fully functional calculator.
why: Building a multi-operation calculator from individual functions demonstrates modular design: each operation lives independently, making the system easy to test, debug, and extend.
analogy: Your calculator is like a kitchen with six specialized appliances. The toaster (add) only toasts. The blender (multiply) only blends. The microwave (power) heats with repeated cycles. Each appliance has one job, works independently, and can be replaced or upgraded without affecting the others. The recipe (main) decides which appliances to use and in what order.
try_it: Add a `percentage(value: Int, percent: Int) -> Int` function that calculates what `percent`% of `value` is (use integer division). Then add `square(n: Int) -> Int` and `cube(n: Int) -> Int` that reuse your `power` function.
tips: power(base, 0) should return 1 — the loop simply doesn't run when exp is 0
Every function has one job — don't make add also print or divide also validate
Handle edge cases inside each function: divide by zero, negative exponents
Name functions as verbs: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, modulus
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle division by zero — crashes the program
Starting result at 0 in power — 0 multiplied by anything is 0, so power always returns 0
Using loop condition i <= exp instead of i < exp — runs one extra time
Writing everything in main() without creating separate functions — defeats the purpose of modular design
